reason: Filmmuseum Potsdam self-publishes its collection on museum-digital (the official German distributed museum-digitisation platform — objects under institution 226 are catalogued/published BY the museum, NOT an aggregator like Europeana), which exposes a clean documented JSON API. The in-scope FLAT film art is the curated collection 5865 'Filmplakate aus der DDR' = 100 DEFA/Progress-era DDR film posters (1945–1990), all object_type 'Filmplakat'. Verified live: every poster has a full-resolution master image (~1000–1029 × ~1450px, ≥600px, full colour, NOT watermarked/placeholder — e.g. Werner Klemke's 1956 'Die kleine Stadt will schlafen gehn') reachable at data/{subset}/{folder}/{filename_loc} on museum-digital's CDN, and rich metadata: title, inventory number, dimensions (cm), production year (event 'Hergestellt'), and a named poster designer (event 'Geistige Schöpfung' — Werner Klemke, Kurt Geffers, Heinz Ebel, Ernst Lauenroth, etc.; 14/15 in probe). The two other institution-226 collections are OUT of scope: 5837 'DDR-Amateurfilme' (97 × 16mm films = moving image) and 1159 'Schriften zur Filmtechnik' (24 × Schriftgut = printed documents/patents). Probe (15 works) passed end-to-end with live R2 uploads; validate-metadata.mjs → REAL fill title/artist/year/category/dimensions 100%, 0 blockers.
easy_source_found: YES — museum-digital JSON API (no auth, documented /swagger). Filmmuseum Potsdam = institution 226 on nat.museum-digital.de (also brandenburg.museum-digital.de inst 8). List: GET /json/objects?s=collection:5865&startwert=N (page size 24, 404 past last record). Detail: GET /json/object/{id}. Full-res image = /data/{md_subset}/{object_images[main].folder}/{filename_loc} (no size prefix; '200w_' prefix is the thumbnail). museum-digital is the museum's OWN self-publishing infra, not a forbidden aggregator. The museum's own www.filmmuseum-potsdam.de site has only a search box (Adlib-backed) with no machine-readable export; museum-digital is the open, published surface. No /opendata|/api|/jsonapi on the .de domain.

exhibitions_entry.name: Filmmuseum Potsdam
exhibitions_entry.description: Germany's oldest film museum, founded in 1981 in the historic Marstall (the former royal stables) by the Sanssouci park in Potsdam, next to the Babelsberg studio. It documents German film history with a special focus on DEFA, the state-owned film studio of the GDR. Its poster collection holds roughly 15,000 film posters — about 9,500 distinct SBZ/GDR posters (1945–1990), largely for the Progress-Film-Verleih distributor — and is regarded as the most important German collection of GDR film posters; a digitised selection is published with the DEFA-Stiftung on the open museum-digital platform.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 1981년에 문을 연 독일에서 가장 오래된 영화박물관으로, 포츠담 상수시 공원 곁의 옛 왕실 마구간 건물(마르슈탈)에 자리하며 바벨스베르크 촬영소와 이웃해 있다. 독일 영화사를 다루되 특히 동독(DDR)의 국영 영화사 DEFA에 무게를 둔다. 약 1만 5천 점의 영화 포스터를 소장하는데, 그중 1945~1990년 동독 시기의 서로 다른 포스터가 약 9,500점으로 대부분 국영 배급사 프로그레스(Progress-Film-Verleih)를 위해 제작된 것이며, 독일 최고의 동독 영화 포스터 컬렉션으로 꼽힌다. 그 가운데 디지털화된 일부가 DEFA 재단과 함께 공개 플랫폼 museum-digital에 게재되어 있다.
